a: Noticing everyday magic and drawing strength from it
Escaping daily life through travel to remote places
Finding a spiritual practice that explains the world
Feeling awe only in the presence of grand landscapes
questions.why: Lesson 1 quotes May's idea that enchantment means noticing everyday magic and drawing strength from it.

questions.q: Which earth practices does May recommend?
a: Walking barefoot and keeping a pebble in your pocket
Gardening every morning and composting at home
Hiking long distances and climbing mountains
Sleeping outdoors and eating only local food
questions.why: Lesson 1 calls walking barefoot a moving meditation and says keeping a pebble in your pocket can calm an anxious mind.

questions.q: Why does May see fire as a gift as well as a danger?
a: Respected, it cooks food and gathers people together
It destroys old forests so new cities can be built
It burns away emotions that cause anxiety
It makes meteor showers visible from Earth
questions.why: Lesson 2 says fire cleanses and renews, lets us cook, and draws people around campfires to tell stories and belong.

questions.q: What does air symbolize for May?
a: Constant change and the chance to try a new direction
The stillness that comes from meditation
The invisible force that holds the sky together
The danger of losing touch with reality
questions.why: Lesson 2 links air to constant change and the freedom to choose a different path.

questions.q: What was aether in early science?
a: An invisible fifth element thought to hold everything together
A gas that scientists believed made up the atmosphere
A measure of how much light a star emits
A type of meteor shower seen only in spring
questions.why: Lesson 3 says early scientists believed aether, or quintessence, was an invisible glue holding the sky, stars and sun together.
